subject: Sprint pact: POC gatekeepers, success tests, and next-step checkins
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@nextgenretail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@itnexgen.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up and initial success signals from today's call

Hi Kimberly and Ben,

Thanks for the demo today — appreciate the clear rundown on routing and the cost controls. Samir and I reviewed internally and we want to scope a short POC to validate latency and throughput for our checkout fraud-detection use-case.

High-level asks from our side:
- Proof that the model can maintain sub-120ms median latency for 1k rps simulated traffic.
- End-to-end data handling confirmation (redaction + retention policy) for PII.
- A minimal success matrix we can share with our security and SRE teams.

Samir will coordinate infra access; I can do a quick handshake call next week to lock dates. Can you send a proposed POC plan and owners?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen
Director, Analytics
NexGen Retail

Date: 2027-05-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and initial success signals from today's call

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a short post-call plan to get the POC moving; I attached a one-sheet success matrix (poc-success-matrix.xlsx) for your security/SRE review.

POC sprint outline (2 weeks, lightweight):
- Week 0 (prep): network allowlist, sample data redaction, baseline perf test (internal infra) — owners: Samir (NexGen), Priyom (Redwood engineering).
- Week 1: Loaded runs against Redwood Dedicated test endpoint, measure median latency and p95 under 1k rps simulated traffic — owner: Ben (Redwood).
- Week 2: Acceptance verification, QA on retention and logs, handover doc. Final decision meeting.

Success gates (short):
- Median latency < 120ms at 1k rps
- No PII persisted in logs / retention configurable to 30 days
- End-to-end call set up with SRE to validate network flows

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Confirm Samir as infra lead + available CIDR ranges for allowlist.
2) Provide a safe sample dataset (anonymized) and preferred time window for the first load run (we recommend Wed or Thu next week).

I attached the success matrix and the network checklist to speed approvals. Ben — can you confirm Redwood's test endpoint and rough time budget for the load runs? Marissa, I'll loop you on scheduling for the validation meeting.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and initial success signals from today's call

Adding some implementation detail — summary for SRE and infra planning.

Test endpoint details:
- Endpoint: https://dedicated-test-01.redwood.test/nextgen (ephemeral creds to follow)
- Expected tokenization overhead: ~8ms per request (baseline for our LLM variant)
- Sim harness: k6 script + synthetic traces (we will share script)

Operational considerations:
- We'll enable prefix KV caching for repeated checkout flows to keep p95 within targets; caching config will be part of the runbook.
- For retention: logs are stored in a segregated bucket and we can configure lifecycle to 30d or less.

Owners and immediate actions:
- Ben Carter (Redwood): runbook, load script, endpoint provisioning (ETA Tue 05/25)
- Priyom Das (Redwood eng): assist on custom headers, authentication, and KV cache tuning
- Samir Patel (NexGen): CIDR & VPN details, sample dataset delivery

Alex — if you can confirm a Wed run (05/26) evening window (PST) we can provision and smoke test earlier that day.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
